locations.name: Red Soil
locations.summary: Odisha's most widely distributed soil — coarse, porous, iron-rich and acidic. Covers the southern and south-western hill belt.

details.coverage: ≈ 7.14 million hectares (largest of all soil groups)
details.formation: Decomposition of silicate and iron deposits of the upper Dharwar series during heavy rainfall.
details.texture: Coarse-textured, highly porous; strongly to moderately acidic.
details.fertility: Rich in iron, potassium and phosphorus; deficient in nitrogen and organic matter.

locations.name: Mixed Red and Yellow Soil
locations.summary: Second-largest soil group. Coarse and acidic in uplands; finer and richer in lowlands.

details.texture: Upland: coarse, acidic. Lowland (on alluvial deposits): finer, richer in potassium.
details.fertility: Lowland variants more productive due to alluvial enrichment.
details.notes: Dominant across western Odisha; the two variants (upland vs. lowland) behave quite differently.

locations.name: Laterite Soil
locations.summary: Deep red, iron-oxide-rich soil formed by intense leaching under tropical monsoon. Strongly acidic and low in fertility.

details.formation: Intense leaching of basaltic rocks and gneisses under tropical monsoon conditions.
details.texture: Deep red to reddish-brown; high iron oxide content; strongly acidic.

locations.name: Deltaic Alluvial Soil
locations.summary: The most fertile soil of Odisha — silt and clay deposited by east-flowing rivers. Excellent moisture retention.

details.formation: Silt and clay deposits laid down by east-flowing rivers (Mahanadi, Brahmani, Baitarani, Subarnarekha).
details.texture: Varies from sandy loam (N. Balasore) to clayey (Mahanadi delta).
details.fertility: Highly fertile; excellent moisture retention; slightly acidic to neutral.

locations.name: Black Soil
locations.summary: Heavy clay soil that swells when wet and cracks deeply in summer. Neutral to alkaline, calcium-rich.

details.texture: Heavy; >30% clay; swells when wet, cracks deeply in summer; neutral to alkaline.
details.fertility: Rich in calcium; deficient in phosphorus and zinc.

locations.name: Mixed Red and Black Soil
locations.summary: Catenary mix — red soil in upper reaches, black soil in lower regions. Medium fertility, neutral pH.

details.texture: Catenary formation: red soil upper, black soil lower; neutral pH.

locations.name: Coastal Saline & Alluvial Soil
locations.summary: Narrow tidal-affected strip (5–25 km) along the coast. Highly alkaline due to salt-water incursion.

details.coverage: Narrow strip 5–25 km wide along the coast
details.notes: Tidal incursion drives the alkalinity; cultivation needs salt-tolerant crop varieties.

locations.name: Brown Forest Soil
locations.summary: Light, acidic, organic-rich soil of the forested hill belt. Threatened by Podu (shifting cultivation).

details.fertility: Rich in organic matter and nitrogen.
details.notes: Frequently subjected to Shifting Cultivation (Podu), which causes degradation and loss of topsoil.
